output.review_comment:
I'm requesting changes: all 10 tests now pass, but only because of a special case added to make one test pass, and the PR changes the documented behaviour without saying why.

1. The midpoint rule exists only to pass one test. The code's normal rule takes the value at floor((p/100)*(n-1)), a method nobody uses. It averages two values only when that position lands exactly on .5. The only thing that needs that branch is test_median_response_time ([120, 80, 200, 150], p50 -> 135). For any other p the result jumps from the lower value to the average and back, and checking a float with == 0.5 is fragile. The new docstring calls this "linear interpolation", but it describes the floor rule, and the code doesn't interpolate either.

2. It drops the agreed spec. The README and the original docstring both say to use nearest-rank, so every reported value is a real sample. The PR rewrote the docstring to match the new code without explaining the change. That changes behaviour the SRE team relies on, and the dashboard's p50/p90/p99 go through this function.

3. The underlying problem wasn't raised. A correct nearest-rank version (value at 1-based rank ceil(p/100*n), smallest value when p is 0) passes 9 of the 10 tests. The one it fails is test_median_response_time: nearest-rank gives 120 there, not 135. That test conflicts with the documented spec, and the PR should have said so instead of hiding it with a special case.

Suggested fix:
- Implement nearest-rank as documented: idx = max(1, math.ceil(p/100*n)), return ordered[idx-1].
- Keep the new check that p is between 0 and 100. That part is a good fix.
- Leave the docstring as it was.
- Tell the teammate or SRE team that test_median_response_time contradicts the nearest-rank spec, and let them decide whether the test or the spec should change. We shouldn't quietly redefine the method.

The PR also has no description, so the change of method isn't explained anywhere.
